intro: The formal letter and email: how to open, state your purpose, ask, and close.

palabras.consejo: With yo the g becomes j: «me dirijo». It is the formal way to start a letter.
It opens a letter: «estimado señor», «estimada señora». It changes gender with the person.
It is written as three words, without «a»: «en relación con su anuncio». It is formal.
It is pronominal: «me pongo en contacto con ustedes». It is very common in letters and emails.
You say «le adjunto mi currículum». An email carries «archivos adjuntos».
It is feminine and ends in -ud: «la solicitud». The stress goes at the end: so-li-thi-TUD.
It is a closing formula. It is said in the first person: «quedo a su disposición».

palabras.palabra: a la espera de sus noticias
palabras.significado: looking forward to hearing from you
palabras.pron: a la es-PE-ra de sus no-TI-thyas
palabras.consejo: It is a formula before the closing. Here «noticias» means «reply or information».
It is an old closing formula. It is used less today: «sin otro particular, le saluda atentamente».
It comes from «atento» plus «-mente». It goes at the end, followed by a comma and your name.
It is the most used closing in emails today. It takes a comma at the end: «un cordial saludo,».
It works for men and women: «el remitente», «la remitente». It goes on the back of the envelope.
It is the opposite of «remitente». Its name goes on the front of the envelope.
In an email it should say clearly what you want. It is masculine: «el asunto».
«empezar» changes e to ie. The c before e sounds like th.
Money given to help study or research. The v sounds like b.
From «investigar», to research. Ends in -ción.
Its opposite is «imposible». The v sounds like b.
From «pedir», to ask. The accent shows the stress on ón.
Its opposite is «informal», relaxed.
Imperfect subjunctive after «que», in polite requests.
Papers with official information. Plural of «documento».
Agrees with «documentos». Its opposite is «innecesarios».
From «cortés», polite. Use it for good manners.
In letters, «quedo a su disposición» means I remain at your service.
«a su disposición» means available to you.
A duplicate of a document. The c before o sounds like k.
From «aclarar», to clarify. Ends in -ción.
«arañar» means to scratch lightly. The ñ sounds like ny.
Its opposite is «lleno», full. The v sounds like b.
Participle of «escribir» in feminine form for «dirección».
Its noun form is «cortesía». The accent marks the stress.
A soft sound, like the wind. From «susurrar».
Agrees with «partes». Its opposite is «distintas».
«en la parte de atrás» means on the back side.
Also means language. The g before u sounds like g.
From «saber», to know. The v-like b: «sabor» has no v sound.

piezas.titulo: The skeleton of a formal letter
texto:
**1. Greeting.** Always followed by a colon, not a comma:

- **Estimado señor García:**
- **Estimados señores:** (when you do not know who will read it)

**2. Purpose.**

- **Me dirijo a usted para** solicitar información.
- **Le escribo en relación con** su anuncio.
- **Me pongo en contacto con ustedes**…

**3. Body.** Use **usted**, the conditional and the imperfect subjunctive:

- **Le agradecería que** me **enviara**…
- **Quisiera saber si**…
- **Le adjunto** mi currículum.

**4. Before closing.**

- **Quedo a su disposición** para cualquier aclaración.
- **A la espera de sus noticias**, le saluda atentamente,

**5. Closing.** With a comma and your name on the next line: **Atentamente,** / **Un cordial saludo,**

In an email, **el asunto** must say clearly what you want. On an envelope, **el destinatario** goes on the front and **el remitente** on the back.

piezas.titulo: The five parts of a letter
texto:
A formal letter has five parts:

- **Greeting**, with a colon: **Estimado señor García:**
- **Purpose**: **me dirijo a usted para** + infinitive; **en relación con** + noun.
- **Body**: **le agradecería que** + imperfect subjunctive; **quisiera saber si** + indicative.
- **Close**: **quedo a su disposición**; **a la espera de sus noticias**.
- **Sign-off**, with a comma: **atentamente,** / **un cordial saludo,**

In an email, **el asunto** sums up the purpose in a few words.

pregunta.texto: Which mark follows the greeting in a formal letter?

opciones.explicacion: Yes: «Estimado señor García:» takes a colon.
The comma goes after the sign-off, not after the greeting.
An exclamation mark is too informal.

piezas.traduccion: Le agradecería que me ____ el formulario.

opciones.explicacion: It is indicative; after «que» here comes the subjunctive.
The future does not work after «que» in a request.

opciones.explicacion: It is a sign-off for family or friends.
It is a spoken, informal goodbye.
